sources.title: Apache Flink Improper Access Control Vulnerability
sources.snippet: Apache Flink: Apache Flink contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows an attacker to read any file on the local filesystem of the JobManager through its REST interface. Required action: Apply mitigations per vendor instructions or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.
supports: CISA KEV identifies CVE-2020-17519 as exploited in the wild.

sources.title: CVE-2018-10583: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: An information disclosure vulnerability occurs when LibreOffice 6.0.3 and Apache OpenOffice Writer 4.1.5 automatically process and initiate an SMB connection embedded in a malicious file, as demonstrated by xlink:href=file://192.168.0.2/test.jpg within an office:document-content element in a .odt XML document.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2018-10583 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

sources.title: CVE-2021-24122: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: When serving resources from a network location using the NTFS file system, Apache Tomcat versions 10.0.0-M1 to 10.0.0-M9, 9.0.0.M1 to 9.0.39, 8.5.0 to 8.5.59 and 7.0.0 to 7.0.106 were susceptible to JSP source code disclosure in some configurations. The root cause was the unexpected behaviour of the JRE API File.getCanonicalPath() which in turn was caused by the inconsistent behaviour of the Windows API (FindFirstFileW) in some circumstances.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2021-24122 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

sources.title: Security - Apache Logging Services
sources.snippet: UNTRUSTED WEB RESEARCH (not PCAP evidence). On this page, we will help you find guidance on security-related issues and access to known vulnerabilities. Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output ... | Webpage excerpt: These instructions can be found in BUILDING.adoc, BUILDING.md, etc. files distributed with the sources. It comprises environment variables, configuration properties, and configuration files. Ensure these resources are transmitted only over confidential channels (e.g., HTTPS, secure file systems). If configuration files use interpolation features (e.g., Log4j Lookups), ensure that only trusted data sources are used. Just as they read from sources, logging systems write to sinks: the destinations to which an appender delivers a formatted log event, such as files, consoles, sockets, databases, and message brokers. For example, a Routing appender may open a file whose path is interpolated from a lookup: selecting that destination is the operator’s decision, and the trustworthiness of any value used to build it is the operator’s responsibility (see the FAQ entry on path traversal). Ensuring that untrusted parties do not have write access to a log destination, such as the directory or file a file appender writes to, is a deployer responsibility, exactly as it is for configuration resources (see Configuration (operator-controlled)).
